text.p: Spartech Corp, which earlier reported a 25 percent rise in first quarter earnings, said Tuesday it expects to produce "excellent results" in 1997.

"Based upon the strength of our current backlog (35 percent greater than this time last year), projected margin improvements resulting from increased production efficiencies, and continuing benefits anticipated from our Portage and Hamelin acquisitions, we believe that Spartech will again produce excellent results in 1997," Bradley Buechler, president, said in a statement.
Spartech earned $18.3 million or $0.73 a share on sales of $391.3 million in fiscal 1996 ended November 2.
For the first quarter ended February 1, earnings of $0.20 a share were up from $0.16 a year ago. Sales increased 30 percent to $113.4 million.

"Spartech posted record net sales, despite one less week in our fiscal 1997 first quarter as compared to last year, with the sales growth primarily due to the company's second half 1996 acquisitions of Portage Industries and the Hamelin Group," Buechler said.
